title: Dependency Injection

validation.research: Fowler's 2004 article establishes the name, external assembly, constructor/setter/interface forms, and the Service Locator and broader Inversion of Control distinctions. Seemann supports composition near the application entry point and container-free composition. Microsoft's official guidelines support lifetime mismatch, resource disposal, and resolved-object thread-safety concerns; its architecture guidance supports dependency direction toward abstractions as distinct from supplying collaborators. Official Python documentation supports structural protocols without runtime enforcement, closing on exceptional exits, and SQLite transaction context management without automatic connection closure. The quotation scenario, example, and diagrams are original teaching material.
validation.python_examples: All three actual article blocks execute and print sqlite 375 and memory 375 on separate lines. Checks verify that the consumer imports only typing, requires its collaborator as a constructor argument, and works with SQLite, memory, and a recording provider without concrete-provider inheritance. Invalid quantities fail before provider calls; zero-cent prices work; invalid prices fail; both real providers raise KeyError for missing products. Provider failure propagates unchanged, protocol annotations do not silently validate arbitrary objects, fixture copies remain independent, and different supplied providers produce independent results. Instrumented real SQLite connections verify query cursor closure, borrowed connections staying open after operations and failures, connection closure on normal scope exit, use-after-close failure, and connection closure when an actual startup quote raises. The validator executes a modified startup fixture to force that exceptional path.

example_limits: Manual constructor injection with standard-library Python, one single-threaded in-memory SQLite connection, and integer-cent unit prices. No DI container, durable storage, concurrent access policy, pricing reservation, automatic fallback, or automatic runtime protocol validation is implemented. The application owns the connection; the adapter owns its per-query cursor and borrows the connection; the consumer borrows the provider. Injection supplies no transaction, synchronization, or security-isolation guarantee.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
